style: Colored-pencil and gouache specimens with exact magnetism concept diagrams
provider: Built-in image generation and deterministic SVG diagrams
note: All artwork is text-free. Native captions define the model: coral denotes north, teal denotes south in magnet and compass diagrams. Colors do not identify real materials or polarity. Object identity and alloy are supplied by the card text, not established by appearance. The coin is a deliberately plain silhouette, not a reproduction of a minted design. Sorting predicts sticking to an ordinary stationary classroom magnet; weak magnetic responses and moving-field effects are outside that activity. Force arrows differ from field-direction arrows as each caption explains. Core rings and field curves are schematic. The split-magnet image is a thought experiment, not an instruction to break magnets. Circuit pictures explain switching and are not build plans; use only the teacher-approved current-limited classroom kit or a non-electrical model. A core can retain magnetism after current stops. Educator review is pending.

assets.caption: For these diagrams, coral denotes north and teal denotes south. Colors are a diagram key, not a test of real magnet polarity. Both poles belong to one magnet.

assets.alt: A bar has a coral left half and a teal right half.

assets.caption: For these diagrams, coral denotes north and teal denotes south. Colors are a diagram key, not a test of real magnet polarity. Both poles belong to one magnet.
assets.prompt: Exact text-free diagram: A bar has a coral left half and a teal right half.
assets.alt: A bar has a coral left half and a teal right half.

assets.caption: Opposite poles face across the gap and attract. Coral denotes north; teal denotes south. Arrows show forces on the magnets, not field lines.
assets.prompt: Exact text-free diagram: Two bar magnets have a teal end facing a coral end; arrows above them point inward.
assets.alt: Two bar magnets have a teal end facing a coral end; arrows above them point inward.

assets.caption: The facing poles are both south in this model, so they repel. Two facing north poles also repel. Hold bar magnets aligned to compare the facing poles.
assets.prompt: Exact text-free diagram: Two bar magnets have teal ends facing each other; arrows above them point outward.
assets.alt: Two bar magnets have teal ends facing each other; arrows above them point outward.

assets.caption: Coral is north and teal is south. Magnetic field direction outside a bar magnet runs from north to south; inside, it returns from south to north. Lines model a continuous field, not physical threads. This is a schematic, not a measured field map.
assets.prompt: Exact text-free diagram: Two curved paths run above and below a coral-and-teal bar, with rightward arrows outside and a leftward arrow inside it.
assets.alt: Two curved paths run above and below a coral-and-teal bar, with rightward arrows outside and a leftward arrow inside it.

assets.caption: A magnet can pull a steel paperclip across an air gap without touching it. The arrow shows force on the clip; it does not show a field-line direction or a measured force size.
assets.prompt: Exact text-free diagram: A paperclip is separated from a bar magnet by a clear gap; an arrow above the clip points toward the magnet.
assets.alt: A paperclip is separated from a bar magnet by a clear gap; an arrow above the clip points toward the magnet.

assets.caption: The closed circuit supplies current to the coil, creating a magnetic field that can hold a steel paperclip. The blue block represents a teacher-approved current-limited supply. This is a concept diagram, not assembly wiring or component specifications.

assets.alt: A closed switch and a blue supply block connect to a continuous coil around a gray core; a paperclip touches the underside of the core.

assets.caption: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge. These arrows show conventional current direction; electron drift in a metal is in the opposite direction. This short segment is not a complete working circuit.

assets.alt: A thick wire runs horizontally with three rightward arrows above it.

assets.alt: A circular compass has a coral needle end pointing upward and a teal end downward; an adjacent arrow points upward.
